chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, by a chain of his, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked to recite 'Say, He is Allah, [the] One' in one breath.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, [the] One - the opening phrase of Surah al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112).
key_terms.نَفَسٍ وَاحِدٍ: One breath - referring to the physical act of exhaling during recitation without pausing to inhale.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic ruling indicating a recommended avoidance.

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to recite Surah Al-Ikhlas in one breath?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the virtue of *tadabbur* (reflection) by discouraging the rapid recitation of Surah al-Ikhlas in a single breath, a practice that risks reducing the chapter to mere mechanical utterance. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on quality and mindfulness over speed, ensuring the reciter fully internalizes the theological weight of Allah's absolute unity before moving to the next verse. Such attention to detail in recitation reflects the broader jurisprudential principle that acts of worship must be performed with presence of heart (*hudhur al-qalb*).
